stem:
Manav simplifies $\dfrac{5^{7}}{5^{3}}$ for counting-number exponents with the same nonzero base.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $\dfrac{5^{7}}{2^{3}}=5^{7-3}$, as if different bases still allowed subtracting exponents.
$\dfrac{5^{3}}{5^{7}}=5^{3-7}$ is covered by the same stated rule for $a>b$ counting exponents with no further condition.
$\dfrac{5^{7}}{5^{3}}=5^{7-3}=5^{4}$, because the bases are the same and nonzero.
The value is $5$, because $5$ is the printed base shown most clearly.

teacher.key_rationale: For the same nonzero base and counting exponents a>b, divide by subtracting exponents: 5^7/5^3=5^4. Different bases and the a>b case boundary are outside that stated rule.
